claim: The doc asserts the label-splitting rule splits at every non-alphanumeric character, at lowercase-to-uppercase changes, before the last capital of an uppercase run followed by lowercase, and between letters and digits, with one plural exception for an uppercase run followed by a single lowercase `s`, and that a label matches when its words contain all of an entry's words consecutively and in order, each optionally carrying a trailing `s` or `es`.
source_excerpt: **How labels match.** SQL Lens splits a column label into words at every character that is not a letter or digit, at lowercase-to-uppercase changes, before the last capital of an uppercase run followed by lowercase letters, and between letters and digits (`password_hash` → password, hash; `APIKey` → api, key; `password2` → password, 2). One exception keeps a plural together: an uppercase run followed by a single lowercase `s` and then a non-letter or the end of the label stays one word (`PINs` → pins). Entries split the same way. A label matches when its words contain all of an entry's words, consecutively and in order; each word may also carry a trailing `s` or `es` (`api_keys`, `PINs`).
verify_against: The word splitter and matcher in src/sqllens/safety/masking.py
